newsitem.title: GERMANY: Tietmeyer to address G7 on G10 banking issues.
newsitem.headline: Tietmeyer to address G7 on G10 banking issues.

text.p: Bundesbank president Hans Tietmeyer said on Saturday that he would report to the meeting of Group of Seven officials in Berlin on Saturday about developments within the G10 discussions on banking issues.
Tietmeyer chairs the group of G10 central bank governors which address such issues.
Tietmeyer said he would be giving the G7 an update on issues such as the optimisation of payment systems and the increasing use of electronic money.
He would also be looking at the question of how to integrate newly industrialised countries into payment networks.

"All these issues are not just subjects for the G10 countries but also for those beyond that group," he said. "We have to be sure we can take other countries into the system without creating problems."
The G7 groups Britain, Canada, France, Germany, Italy, Japan and the United States.
The G10 comprises these countries plus four others -- Belgium, Netherlands, Switzerland and Sweden.
